title: Book Three · Chapter 57: Kai's Light
story:
The next day, Ronan and Kai spend lunch on one maths question.

Kai draws the wall quickly. He takes longer with the words below it. Ronan waits until he finishes, then asks him to explain the drawing aloud.

That part is easier. Kai points, talks, and changes one number himself.

“There,” Ronan says.

Kai puts down his pencil. “Enough walls for today.”

In the afternoon, the science teacher brings out batteries, small bulbs, wires, and switches.

They will make a simple path for electricity. Then they need to explain the switch.

Kai moves his chair closer at once. He sorts the parts and puts the battery beside the bulb.

Ronan reads the short sheet. Before he reaches the last line, Kai has joined two wires.

“Hold this end,” Kai says.

Ronan holds it against the metal point. Kai moves the little switch. The bulb lights.

He moves the switch again. The light goes out.

Across the room, another pair is still finding the right ends of the wires. Kai shows them the two metal points, then returns to his own desk.

Anna looks over from her pair's work.

“Already?”

Kai opens the switch and points to the gap.

“Here. Open.”

He closes it again. The bulb lights.

Ronan takes his hand away from the wire too soon. The light goes out at once.

Kai looks at him.

“Another switch.”

Ronan laughs and puts the wire back.

The teacher asks everyone to leave the parts on the desk and write an answer. How does the switch control the light?

Kai writes three words. Then he crosses out two of them.

Ronan looks at his own page. He knows the path needs to be complete. He can say that. Writing it clearly takes more time.

The teacher stops at their desk.

Kai shows the light again. His hands move easily. When the teacher asks about the answer, his fingers stop.

“I can show it,” he says.

“Tell me first,” the teacher says.

Kai points to the switch.

“Open. A gap. The light goes out.”

“Those are your first three steps. Put them on the page.”

Kai looks down. He starts a sentence, then rubs out one word.

The bell rings before he finishes. The teacher tells them to complete the answer at home.

Ronan helps put the parts back in the box. Kai keeps his unfinished page beside his hand.

“My light is faster than my pencil,” he says.

“Mine is slower than both.”

Kai laughs. He puts his answer in his book, carefully away from the loose wires.

He keeps one little drawing of the switch beside the words.

Ronan carries the box to the front. Behind him, Kai reads his first sentence again before he puts the pencil away.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

battery＝电池；bulb＝小灯泡；switch＝开关；gap＝间隙、断开的地方。

## 理解问题

1. Kai在哪一部分表现熟练？他真正觉得困难的又是哪一部分？
2. 小灯泡熄灭只发生在拨开开关时吗？Ronan的动作还造成了什么变化？

## 读句子

**The light goes out at once.**

拆开看：The light / goes out / at once.

灯／熄灭／立刻。
